accepted.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Based on the scenario in (a), explain how the Samy worm propagated and infected MySpace profiles, and describe the impact of this malware on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected systems.

marking_points.point: The Samy worm injected JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It obtained the list of a user's heroes by performing a GET on a user profile.

marking_points.point: It added Samy as a friend by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected profile would get their profile infected with JavaScript and their friends list infected with Samy.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user's page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The worm eventually infected about 1,000,000 MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The worm's propagation relied on the fact that any web application returning user input without filtering is a potential XSS vulnerability.

questions.question: Discuss the professional code of ethics and conduct that computing professionals should follow, as outlined by the ACM.

marking_points.point: Computing professionals should strive to achieve high quality in both processes and products of professional work.
marking_points.quote: Strive to achieve high quality in both the processes and products of professional work.

marking_points.point: They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice.
marking_points.quote: Maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice.

marking_points.point: They should know and respect existing rules pertaining to professional work.
marking_points.quote: Know and respect existing rules pertaining to professional work.

marking_points.point: They should accept and provide appropriate professional review.
marking_points.quote: Accept and provide appropriate professional review.

marking_points.point: They should give comprehensive and thorough evaluations of computer systems and their impacts, including analysis of possible risks.
marking_points.quote: Give comprehensive and thorough evaluations of computer systems and their impacts, including analysis of possible risks.

marking_points.point: They should perform work only in areas of competence.
marking_points.quote: Perform work only in areas of competence.

questions.question: Explain six ways in which an organization's responsibility for privacy is reflected in the ethical codes of professional bodies such as the ACM, AITP, IEEE-CS, and PMI.

marking_points.point: The ACM code of ethics and professional conduct is an example of a documented set of acceptable behaviors for a professional group.
marking_points.quote: Association of Computing Machinery ACM (founded 1947) has a code of ethics and professional conduct.

marking_points.point: The AITP provides quality IT-related education and forums for networking, which support professional conduct in privacy matters.
marking_points.quote: Association of Information Technology Professionals AITP (founded 1996) – provides quality IT-related education, information on relevant IT issues, and forums for networking with experienced peers and other IT professionals.

marking_points.point: The IEEE-CS is another professional body with a code of ethics relevant to computing professionals.
marking_points.quote: Computer Society of the Institute of Electrical and Electronics Engineers (IEEE – CS) (founded in 1946).

marking_points.point: The PMI also has ethical standards that guide project management professionals.
marking_points.quote: Project Management Institute (PMI) – established in 1969.

marking_points.point: Ethics are defined by the group, meaning an organization's responsibility for privacy is shaped by its professional community.
marking_points.quote: Documented set of acceptable behaviors for professional or social groups.

marking_points.point: Ethics identify specific actions as appropriate or inappropriate, which guides an organization's privacy practices.
marking_points.quote: Identifies specific actions as appropriate or inappropriate.

questions.question: Describe the two primary system components of the Next Generation Secure Computing Base (NGSCB), including the functionality of each.

marking_points.point: The two primary system components are Nexus and Nexus Computing Agent (NCA).
marking_points.quote: Two primary system components Nexus Special kernel (core of the trusted operating) Nexus Computing Agent (NCA)

marking_points.point: Nexus is a security kernel that is authenticated on boot.
marking_points.quote: Security kernel, authenticated on boot

marking_points.point: Nexus authenticates trusted programs.
marking_points.quote: Authenticates trusted programs

marking_points.point: Nexus provides an application interface to the TPM.
marking_points.quote: Application interface to TPM

marking_points.point: Nexus does not trust the OS.
marking_points.quote: Does not trust OS

marking_points.point: The Nexus Computing Agent is a trusted software component that runs in trusted mode and communicates with Nexus.
marking_points.quote: Trusted software component Runs in trusted mode that communicates with Nexus

questions.question: Describe the three principal access control structures used to implement access control policies, and for each structure state one advantage or disadvantage.

marking_points.point: Access control matrix (ACM) is a basic control structure with the advantage of clarity of definition.
marking_points.quote: ACM is a basic control structure. Advantages: clarity of definition

marking_points.point: Access control list (ACL) is an object-centered description of access rights, with the advantage of easy access to object access rights.
marking_points.quote: ACL is an object-centered description of access rights:

marking_points.point: Capabilities (C-List) are one of the access control structures listed as mechanisms for implementing access policies.
marking_points.quote: Capabilities (C-List)

marking_points.point: ACLs have the disadvantage of difficulty of revocation.
marking_points.quote: difficulty of revocation

marking_points.point: ACM has the disadvantage of poor scalability.
marking_points.quote: poor scalability

marking_points.point: Capabilities are supported by only a small subset of UNIX-like operating systems, which is a limitation.
marking_points.quote: Capabilities are supported by only a small subset of UNIX-like operating systems

questions.question: Compare the security mechanisms of Windows and UNIX by describing three distinct Windows security mechanisms and three distinct UNIX security mechanisms.

marking_points.point: Windows uses Active Directory, an LDAP-like directory service for organizing system resources.
marking_points.quote: Active directory introduced in Windows 2000 is an LDAP-like directory service for organization of system resources:

marking_points.point: Windows stores security-related information in a hierarchical registry database.
marking_points.quote: A hierarchical database containing critical system information

marking_points.point: Windows subjects are processes and threads with security credentials stored in tokens.
marking_points.quote: Windows subjects are processes and threads. Security credentials for a subject are stored in a token.

marking_points.point: UNIX provides controlled invocation via a special flag allowing programs to run with the owner's privilege.
marking_points.quote: Solution: set a special ﬂag indicating that a program can be run under the privilege of its owner rather than that of a calling user.

marking_points.point: UNIX allows secure mounting of file systems with options like nosuid and noexec.
marking_points.quote: -o nosuid : turn off SUID ﬂags for all data in a mounted ﬁle system

marking_points.point: UNIX provides flexible security mechanisms but lacks features like ACLs and mandatory access control.
marking_points.quote: UNIX provides a set of ﬂexible security mechanisms; however, their efﬁcacy relies on careful and knowledgable administration.

questions.question: Discuss the preventive network security mechanisms of firewalls and VPNs, including their roles and limitations.

marking_points.point: Firewalls control incoming and outgoing traffic based on predetermined security policies.
marking_points.quote: Control incoming and outgoing traffic on network with predetermined security policies.

marking_points.point: Remote Access VPN provides secure remote access to an organization's network for individual hosts or clients.
marking_points.quote: Provides remote and secure access to an organization network to individual hosts or clients

marking_points.point: Zero Trust Network Access (ZTNA) ensures a user only has access and permission required to fulfill their role.
marking_points.quote: A user should only has access and permission that required to fulfill the role

marking_points.point: IDS/IPS are preventive mechanisms that detect or prevent attacks such as brute force, DoS, and exploits of network vulnerabilities.
marking_points.quote: To detect or prevent the network security attacks such as brute force attacks, Denial-of-Service attacks and exploits of network vulnerabilities.

marking_points.point: Network segmentation creates boundaries between segments where assets share a common function, risk, or role.
marking_points.quote: Boundaries between network segments where computing assets within the segment have a common function, risk or role within an organization.

marking_points.point: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.
marking_points.quote: Proxy servers act as a firewall and web filter, provide shared network connections, and cache data to speed up common requests.

questions.question: Refer to your answer in (a). Based on the scenario in (a), explain how the Samy worm propagated and infected MySpace profiles, and describe the impact of this malware on the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the affected systems.

marking_points.point: The Samy worm injected JavaScript into a user profile using document.body.innerHTML.
marking_points.quote: Inject Javascript into a user proﬁle using document.body.innerHTML

marking_points.point: It obtained the list of a user's heroes by performing a GET on a user profile.
marking_points.quote: Get the list of user’s heros by using a GET on a user proﬁle

marking_points.point: It added Samy as a friend by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page.
marking_points.quote: Add Samy as a ﬁeld by performing XML-HTTP on the addFriends page

marking_points.point: Any user visiting an infected profile would get their profile infected with JavaScript and their friends list infected with Samy.
marking_points.quote: Any user who visits an infected user’s page will gets proﬁle infected with Javascript and his friends list infected with Samy

marking_points.point: The worm eventually infected about 1,000,000 MySpace profiles.
marking_points.quote: Eventually about 1,000,000 MySpace proﬁles were infected.

marking_points.point: The worm's propagation relied on the fact that any web application returning user input without filtering is a potential XSS vulnerability.
marking_points.quote: Any web application that returns user input without ﬁltering is a potential XSS vulnerability!

questions.question: State six distinct threat classes described in the lecture slides, and for each, state one countermeasure that addresses it.

marking_points.point: Disclosure is a threat class; confidentiality services counter it.

marking_points.point: Deception is a threat class; integrity services counter it.

marking_points.point: Disruption is a threat class; integrity services counter it.

marking_points.point: Usurpation is a threat class; availability services counter it.

marking_points.quote: Vulnerability: weakness of a system

marking_points.point: A threat is a potential violation of security.
